analytics.name: Analytic 1808
analytics.guidance: The defender correlates Android camera access by an app identity with app and device context showing that the capture is inconsistent with expected user-driven recording behavior. The strongest Android evidence is camera resource access followed by sustained capture duration, video or image artifact creation, buffer or cache growth, and optional outbound transfer, especially when the app is backgrounded, operating as a foreground service without visible user initiation, active while the device is locked, or capturing without recent user interaction. The detection is strengthened when the app is unmanaged, recently granted camera access, or not approved to record video.

tuning.description: Correlation window linking camera access, lifecycle context, artifact creation, and optional network transfer.
Minimum sustained camera session duration considered unusual for the app role.
Approved camera-capable apps vary by organization, device group, and role.
Some apps should only access the camera while visibly foregrounded.
Defines how close camera activation must be to user interaction to be considered expected.
Specific enterprise or accessibility workflows may legitimately capture while not foregrounded.
Minimum media-buffer or file-write volume indicating probable video or burst-image capture.
Threshold for suspicious outbound transfer after capture.

analytics.name: Analytic 1809
analytics.guidance: The defender correlates managed-app or supervised-device camera access with app and device context showing that the capture is inconsistent with expected user-driven recording behavior. The strongest iOS evidence is camera access or camera-adjacent capture activity followed by app-state evidence such as background or low-interaction operation, optional media artifact creation, and optional post-capture network transfer. Because direct low-level runtime visibility is weaker than Android for many enterprises, the primary iOS analytic should anchor on managed app context, device state, and downstream effects around camera use, with local subsystem telemetry treated as enrichment rather than sole proof.

tuning.description: Correlation window linking camera access, device state, artifact creation, and optional network transfer.
Minimum sustained camera session duration considered unusual for the bundle role.
Strongest bundle-baseline and managed-app analytics depend on supervised iOS devices.
Approved managed bundle identities with camera capability vary by organization and device profile.
Some managed apps should only access the camera during visible foreground use.
Defines how close camera activation must be to user interaction to be considered expected.
Specific approved workflows may legitimately capture media under constrained background-like conditions.
